correctness.rationale: For additive character psi, Fourier-transform target counts by the nondegenerate skew trace pairing. The sum over symmetric Y is q^6 precisely when [Z,X]=0, giving Fhat(Z)=q^(6+d(Z)). Every nonzero skew 3x3 Z has rank two, Z^2 nonzero, and degree-three minimal polynomial, hence full centralizer k[Z]; its symmetric subspace is span{I,Z^2}, so d(Z)=2, whereas d(0)=6. Fourier inversion on the q^3 skew targets gives exactly the two formulas and total q^12 pairs. At n4, Z1=J⊕0 and Z2=J⊕tJ (t^2!=1) have symmetric-centralizer dimensions four and two, so nonzero Fourier frequencies are unequal and target uniformity is impossible. Independently exhaustive F3 enumeration of all 3^12 ordered symmetric pairs yielded zero fiber 26001 and each of 26 nonzero fibers 19440.
residual_risks: The dimension-four obstruction requires q>=5 and does not assert q=3; characteristic two excluded by trace pairing.
Brute-force F3 confirms the special case, not all prime powers.

value.rationale: The bracket map Sym3×Sym3→Skew3 is a natural symmetric-pair quadratic map with a multivariate target. Uniform nonzero fibers for all odd fields, exact commuting probability q^-3+q^-4-q^-7, and its sharp dimension-four obstruction reveal a structural low-dimensional centralizer rigidity absent in general higher-dimensional settings.
residual_risks: Does not classify all n4 fibers or characteristic-two behavior.

final_claim: For each odd prime power q and skew C in M3(F_q), ordered symmetric commutator fibers have size q^9+q^8-q^5 for C=0 and q^9-q^5 otherwise; the constant-nonzero behavior breaks at n=4 for q>=5.
limitations: All odd prime powers; n4 only obstruction q>=5; no all-n target classification.
